findings.title: The argued-cap entry says round 3's three fixes were 'all deleted rather than rewritten', and the recorded trees show one of them was a rewrite that added the claim this very round deletes
findings.summary: The staged `rounds:M4.10a` line reads: 'ROUND 3 WAS THREE FALSE CLAIMS OF MINE, all deleted rather than rewritten, because in M0.76 every round's fix produced the next round's finding and a deletion cannot add a claim'. MEASURED against the trees the harness recorded with each verdict -- `git diff e63855ef 36fd2017 -- sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/CommitProtocolSimulationFlushSeqTest.java`: two of the three were deletions (the method-javadoc sentence 'The defect needs a FAILED commit...' was removed with nothing put in its place; the `### M4.10a` notes section was removed), but the third was a REWRITE that added two new claims. Round 3 replaced 'THIS IS THE TEST THAT KILLS A SHARED COUNTER. Uniqueness above passes against one; density from zero per pod, and two pods colliding on a value within a single seed, cannot.' with 'The shared-value count is this test's ANTI-VACUITY GUARD and not a second discriminator', and rewrote the class javadoc's 'What separates the two is DENSITY and OVERLAP' into 'DENSITY is what separates them: per pod the sequence is exactly 0..n-1, which one shared counter cannot produce.' The round-3 test-reviewer then found the first of those new claims wrong under mutation, and deleting it is item two of THIS round's delta. So the entry's stated reason for convergence is refuted by the round it is written in: round 3's fix did add a claim, and that claim bought round 4 -- the exact M0.76 pathology the sentence claims was avoided. (The second added claim, 'which one shared counter cannot produce', is still in the tree and the round-3 test-reviewer recorded that it holds of the sweep but not of the 11 single-issuing-pod seeds; it is unchanged this round and I am not re-opening it.)
findings.failure_scenario: baselines/review.txt is the tree's only durable record of what going past the cap bought, and review.md rule `two-round-cap` makes that record the thing an argued exception buys over a silent SKIP. A future author at the cap greps `rounds:` for precedent, reads that this task's rounds converged because every fix was a deletion, and concludes that the delete-don't-rewrite policy was applied and worked here. The truth available from the same task is the more useful lesson and the opposite one: one of the three fixes was a rewrite, the rewrite added a claim, the claim was measured wrong, and it cost a fourth round. The entry as written also understates this task's round count for anyone reasoning about the escape's cost. Minimal remedy, and it is itself a deletion so it cannot add a claim: drop the clause 'all deleted rather than rewritten, because in M0.76 every round's fix produced the next round's finding and a deletion cannot add a claim', leaving 'ROUND 3 WAS THREE FALSE CLAIMS OF MINE'. I am NOT asking for that this round -- review.md rule `minors-land` applies, and rule `two-round-cap`'s own tail plus the packet's warning say the next round's surface is the prose the fix adds. Record it in the commit body or harvest it at the milestone boundary (`minors-at-milestone`).

findings.title: The replacement sentence names 'THE DRIVER' with no antecedent in the M4.10 row and drops the only pointer telling M4.10 where its dedup gets exercised
findings.summary: The three falsified clauses are correctly gone and the substitute is true, but one non-falsified fact went with them. The deleted text said '...it has to land before this row's dedup can be tested at all', which was the only sentence in M4.10's notes identifying the simulation as the vehicle that exercises the dedup, and the deleted middle clause carried the still-true fact that 'a zombie's pod name can be re-picked as the next leader from three names'. What replaces them is 'THE DRIVER'S `flushSeq` ISSUANCE WAS FIXED IN M4.10a: per pod, per attempt', in a row that never otherwise says 'simulation' or 'driver' -- so the referent resolves only by opening backlog-done.md, which AGENTS.md does not send a session to ('read the notes for the ONE task you pick'). Both facts do survive in the backlog-done.md M4.10a row, which is why this is minor and not major.
findings.failure_scenario: A session picks M4.10, reads this row per AGENTS.md, and learns that the pair is not durable across a process start and that some 'driver' was fixed. It does not learn that CommitProtocolSimulation is where a (podId, flushSeq) dedup would be exercised, nor that the harness's allocator is keyed on pod NAME for the whole run -- so a pod name re-picked as leader continues one monotone sequence instead of restarting at 0, and the restart-at-0 collision this row names as its primary hazard is not reproducible there today. The session builds `lastAppliedFlushSeq` against unit fixtures, reports it verified, and the one harness that could have exercised it is never touched; or it does model a restart and finds that CommitProtocolSimulationFlushSeqTest's `isEqualTo(expected)` density assertion must be relaxed, with nothing in M4.10's notes saying that was foreseen (non-negotiable 2 makes that an awkward conversation, as round 2's F8 already observed). Remedy, when M4.10 is picked rather than now: restore 'a zombie's pod name can be re-picked as the next leader' and name `CommitProtocolSimulation` explicitly in the sentence. NOT to be fixed this round -- `minors-land`, and editing this row again is another hash and another pair of reviewers.
